listings.name: Ohio income tax deduction for active-duty military pay received while stationed outside Ohio
listings.summary: Ohio lets taxpayers deduct military pay and allowances for active-duty service in the armed forces, including the reserve components and the National Guard, when that pay is in federal adjusted gross income. Pay received while stationed in Ohio does not qualify.
listings.eligibility: Members of the U.S. armed forces, reserve components or National Guard who receive active-duty military pay and allowances during the tax year while stationed outside Ohio. Pay received while stationed in Ohio cannot be deducted.
listings.how_to_apply: Claim the deduction when you file your Ohio IT 1040 income tax return. Questions go to the Department of Taxation's military line, 800-282-1780, or Military-Info@tax.state.oh.us.
listings.deadline: With your Ohio income tax return each year
listings.location: Online or by mail
listings.source_title: Ohio Revised Code Section 5747.01 (Definitions), codes.ohio.gov
listings.notes: Verified from the official Ohio Revised Code page on codes.ohio.gov, section 5747.01 division (A)(21) (effective March 5, 2026; latest legislation Senate Bill 9, 136th General Assembly), which states the deduction and the bar on pay received while stationed in Ohio. Phone, email and the IT 1040 filing advice come from tax.ohio.gov/individual/military, also read. The tax.ohio.gov military FAQ still refused our fetch, so the earlier detail about temporary training of 30 days or less, the Schedule of Adjustments line, and the nonresident rule were dropped because no page we read states them.

listings.name: Athens Area Stand Down
listings.organization: Athens Area Stand Down (community committee, with Ohio University volunteers among its partners)
listings.summary: A yearly one-day stand down at the Athens County Fairgrounds for veterans and community members who are homeless or at risk of homelessness, handing out winter items such as hats, jackets, gloves, blankets, toiletries and socks, with agencies on site sharing other resources.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and community members who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Veterans are served for the full event (10 a.m. to 2 p.m.); others in need are admitted from noon.
listings.how_to_apply: Come on event day. Veterans enter the main gate and check in at the tents; a side-by-side vehicle carries people with limited mobility, and Athens on Demand (HAPCAP) offers free rides for people not on a bus route (740-597-2404 to schedule).
listings.deadline: Held once a year in early fall. The 2026 stand down was Friday, October 2, 2026, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.; the 2027 date is not yet published.
listings.location: Athens County Fairgrounds, 286 W. Union St., Athens, OH
listings.source_title: Athens Area Stand Down for Homeless or At Risk of Being Homeless
listings.notes: Read the event's own site, athensareastanddown.org (linked from the Ohio University article), which gives the October 2, 2026 date, hours, place, who is served and arrival rules. The street address and the veterans-first hours also come from the Ohio University article (ohio.edu, October 1, 2024), read in full. The 2026 event has passed; recheck the site in late summer 2027 for the next date. No event phone is published.

listings.name: Veteran (Armed Forces) designation on Ohio driver license or ID
listings.summary: Adds a military emblem to your Ohio driver license or state ID so you can show veteran status without carrying your DD-214. Adding the emblem itself is free.
listings.eligibility: Any veteran, active-duty or reserve member of the U.S. armed forces.
listings.how_to_apply: Ask for the designation when you renew, get a duplicate or apply in person, online or by mail; show a DD-214, military ID, county veteran ID card or current orders once.
listings.location: BMV deputy registrar license agencies, online or by mail
listings.cost: Free to add; normal license or ID fees apply if you need a new card
listings.source_title: Armed Forces Designation - Ohio BMV

listings.name: Veteran with Disabilities license plates
listings.summary: Free disabled veteran license plates for veterans rated 100% service-connected disabled or who received a VA vehicle allowance; eligible veterans may not have to pay registration fees.
listings.eligibility: Veteran with a VA service-connected disability rated or compensated at 100%, or who received a VA monetary allowance toward a vehicle for service-connected disabilities. Passenger vehicles, non-commercial trucks, motorcycles, motorhomes and non-commercial trailers.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit form BMV 4507 with a VA letter dated within the past year showing 100% (or proof of the vehicle allowance) at a deputy registrar license agency or by mail to BMV Registration Support Services.
listings.location: BMV deputy registrar license agencies or by mail
listings.cost: No additional fees; eligible veterans may not be required to pay registration fees
listings.source_title: Veterans with Disabilities Plates - Ohio BMV
listings.notes: Holders of these plates also qualify for free Ohio hunting and fishing licenses (ORC 1533.12).

listings.name: Former Prisoner of War license plates
listings.summary: Free license plates for former prisoners of war and their surviving spouses.
listings.eligibility: U.S. service members who were imprisoned by an enemy of the United States, or their spouses (spouses also provide a death certificate).
listings.how_to_apply: Submit form BMV 4507 with proof of POW status (service records, War Claims Commission or VA letter) at a deputy registrar or by mail.
listings.location: BMV deputy registrar license agencies or by mail
listings.source_title: Military and veteran license plates - Ohio BMV

listings.name: Gold Star Family license plate
listings.summary: A specialty license plate honoring the family of a service member who died in a combat zone, with no additional fees beyond regular registration.
listings.eligibility: Any member of the immediate family of a person who died in a combat zone while a member of any branch of the armed forces. Available for passenger vehicles, non-commercial trucks, recreational vehicles, house vehicles and non-commercial trailers.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit form BMV 4635 verifying your relationship to the military family member. Plates are ordered at a deputy registrar license agency, online through OPLATES.com, or by mail to the address on your renewal notice.
listings.location: BMV deputy registrar license agencies, online or by mail
listings.cost: No additional fees beyond regular registration
listings.source_title: Ohio BMV
listings.notes: Read the BMV specialty plate information page (Gold Star Family entry, Ohio Revised Code 4503.546). Phone is the general BMV line from bmv.ohio.gov/military-veteran-license-plates.aspx, also read. The same page lists a separate Military Sacrifice plate (form BMV 4817, ORC 4503.549, no additional fees) for families of service members who died outside a combat zone; it could be a separate listing.

listings.name: Free driver license for 100% disabled veterans
listings.summary: Veterans with a 100% service-connected disability rating get their Ohio driver license (new, renewal or duplicate) at no cost.
listings.eligibility: U.S. armed forces veteran with a 100% service-connected disability rating from the VA who is otherwise eligible for an Ohio driver license.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply in person at a BMV deputy registrar license agency with a VA letter dated within the past year showing the 100% rating, or a DoD ID identifying you as a 100% disabled veteran; bring it to every license transaction.
listings.location: BMV deputy registrar license agencies
listings.source_title: Gratis Driver License 100% Service-connected Disability Rating - Ohio BMV

listings.name: Congressional Medal of Honor license plates
listings.summary: Free license plates for Medal of Honor recipients (Army, Navy, Air Force versions).
listings.eligibility: Recipients of the Congressional Medal of Honor.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit form BMV 4507 with documentary evidence of the award at a deputy registrar or by mail.
listings.location: BMV deputy registrar license agencies or by mail
listings.source_title: Military and veteran license plates - Ohio BMV

listings.name: Purple Heart and Purple Heart Disability license plates
listings.summary: No-fee Purple Heart license plates for Purple Heart recipients, and a Purple Heart Disability plate for recipients who are also 100% service-connected disabled or received a VA vehicle allowance.
listings.eligibility: Purple Heart recipients (DD-214 or award certificate). Disability version also requires a 100% VA service-connected rating or a VA vehicle purchase allowance.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit a copy of the DD-214 showing the award (and for the disability version form BMV 4705 and a VA letter dated within the past year) at a deputy registrar or by mail.
listings.location: BMV deputy registrar license agencies or by mail
listings.cost: No fees (Purple Heart); Purple Heart Disability has no additional fees except $1.00 on transfers
listings.source_title: Military and veteran license plates - Ohio BMV
listings.notes: Purple Heart Disability details from the Veterans with Disabilities Plates page (read).

listings.name: Veteran, service, medal and campaign license plates
listings.summary: Dozens of military license plates with no additional plate fee: honorably discharged veteran plates for each branch, women veterans plates, retired, Guard and Reserve plates, medal and badge plates (Bronze Star, Silver Star, Combat Action Ribbon and more), and campaign plates (Korea, Vietnam, Lebanon, Grenada, Panama, Persian Gulf, Somalia, Pearl Harbor).
listings.eligibility: Depends on the plate: a DD-214, Certificate of Honorable Discharge or county veteran ID for veteran plates; DD-214 or award certificate showing the medal for medal plates; proof of in-country service dates for campaign plates.
listings.how_to_apply: Order at a BMV deputy registrar license agency or by mail with the listed proof for the plate you want.
listings.location: BMV deputy registrar license agencies or by mail
listings.cost: No additional plate fees (regular registration fees apply)
listings.source_title: Military and veteran license plates - Ohio BMV
listings.notes: Organization plates (American Legion, DAV, Gold Star Family, Folds of Honor, Marine Corps League, POW-MIA, Military Sacrifice, Support Our Troops) are listed separately on the BMV organizational plates section, not read; their fees were not verified.

listings.name: CDL testing waivers for military drivers and recent veterans
listings.summary: Service members and veterans separated within 12 months who drove a truck-equivalent vehicle in the military can skip the CDL knowledge test (Military Even Exchange) and/or the skills test (Military Skills Test Waiver).
listings.eligibility: On active duty or separated within the past 12 months, and in the last 12 months held a military job operating a vehicle equivalent to a commercial motor vehicle (for example Army 88M, 92F, 14T; Air Force 2T1, 2F0, 3E2; Marine Corps 3531; Navy EO). Skills waiver also requires a valid Ohio driver license. Initial CDL only.
listings.how_to_apply: Bring form BMV 2071 (knowledge test) and/or BMV 2070 (skills test), your license, two-year driving record, DD-214 or military ID, Operator Qualification Record and Military Motor Vehicle Operator's ID card to a driver exam station.
listings.location: Ohio BMV driver exam stations
listings.source_title: CDL Testing Waivers Within 12 Months Separation - Ohio BMV

listings.name: Central Ohio Veterans Stand Down
listings.summary: Free one-day event at the Greater Columbus Convention Center with food, new clothing, VA health screenings, VA and Social Security benefits counseling, and referrals for housing, jobs, treatment and education.
listings.eligibility: Veterans. Walk-ins welcome with a military ID; lunch is free for veteran guests.
listings.how_to_apply: Pre-register with the Veteran Pre-Intake Registration form on the Stand Down website once registration opens (it opened in August for the 2026 event), or walk in with military ID.
listings.deadline: Held each fall (latest was Oct. 23, 2026). 2027 date not yet published.
listings.location: Greater Columbus Convention Center, 400 N. High St., Columbus
listings.source_title: Veterans Stand Down - Franklin County, Ohio
listings.notes: Services list is from the county's 2025 event page; the organizer's site says 'We will see you again in 2027.' Open to central Ohio veterans, not only Franklin County. Contact CentralOhiostandDown@gmail.com.

listings.name: Veterans' preference on Ohio civil service exams
listings.summary: Veterans who pass an Ohio civil service exam get an extra 20% of their total grade added; Reserve and Guard members in good standing who finished initial training get 15%.
listings.eligibility: Ohio residents who completed uniformed service and were honorably discharged or transferred to the reserve with satisfactory service (Reserve and Guard members qualify with more than 180 days of active duty) get 20%. Reserve members in good standing who completed initial entry-level training get 15%. Credit applies only to a passing grade; you cannot get both.
listings.how_to_apply: File your certificate of service or honorable discharge (DD-214) with the Ohio Department of Administrative Services when you apply for a civil service exam.
listings.location: Ohio state civil service hiring
listings.source_title: Section 124.23 - Ohio Revised Code (examinations; veterans' additional credit)
listings.notes: Apply URL is the statute because the state jobs site was not read; current version effective March 20, 2025.

listings.name: College credit for military training and experience
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Higher Education and Ohio public colleges
listings.summary: Ohio's public colleges and universities have committed to accept and award college credit for military training, experience and coursework, with a statewide tool that shows what your training transfers as.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and service members with military training, experience or coursework (for example on a Joint Services Transcript).
listings.how_to_apply: Send your Joint Services Transcript to your Ohio public college and ask the veterans or registrar office for a military credit review; check expected credit with the Ohio Transfer to Degree Guarantee military tool.
listings.location: Ohio public colleges and universities; online lookup tool
listings.source_title: Education For Veterans - Ohio Department of Higher Education

listings.name: Columbus Zoo military discount
listings.summary: $4 off admission on up to six tickets with a valid military ID at the front gate.
listings.eligibility: Active and non-active duty military personnel with valid military ID. The page does not name veterans or retirees separately.
listings.how_to_apply: Show a valid military ID at the Zoo front gate. Not available online.
listings.location: Columbus Zoo and Aquarium, Powell, OH
listings.source_title: Columbus Zoo | Discounts
listings.notes: Whether a veteran without a military ID qualifies is not stated.

listings.name: ODNR controlled hunt lotteries, including mobility-impaired hunts
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife
listings.summary: Each July, ODNR runs lotteries for controlled deer, waterfowl and other hunts on areas not normally open to hunting, including hunts set aside for mobility-impaired hunters (for example deer hunts at Ottawa National Wildlife Refuge, Killdeer Plains Wildlife Area and Castalia Hatchery).
listings.eligibility: Licensed hunters; mobility-impaired hunts are for people unable to move about without crutches, a wheelchair or other support, or whose ability to walk, climb, sit or rise is limited.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply July 1 to July 31 at wildohio.gov, in the HuntFish OH app, or by phone at 866-703-1928 (convenience fee). Winners are drawn at random and notified the week after the window closes.
listings.deadline: Applications July 1 to July 31 each year
listings.location: Designated wildlife areas and refuges statewide
listings.source_title: Controlled Hunting Access Lotteries - Ohio Department of Natural Resources
listings.notes: ODNR pages refused our fetches; details from search excerpts of the lottery page and a July 2026 ODNR release, plus the July 1-31 window and phone line from an ODNR hunting regulations PDF we read (that PDF served 2022 content). A 'Buck Creek State Park - Veterans' archery hunt appeared in an excerpt but could not be confirmed. ODNR did not publish applicant or draw counts in anything we could read.

listings.name: COSI military discount
listings.summary: $2 off general admission per person in the immediate family for military members.
listings.eligibility: Active, Reserve and Retired military members with proper ID.
listings.how_to_apply: Show proper ID when buying admission.
listings.location: COSI, Columbus, OH
listings.cost: $2 off per person in the immediate family
listings.source_title: General Admission Promotions & Discounts | COSI
listings.notes: Veterans who are not retirees are not named.

listings.name: County Veteran ID Card
listings.organization: County Recorder or County Veterans Service Office (participating Ohio counties)
listings.summary: A wallet ID card from your county that proves veteran status, so you do not need to carry your DD-214 to get veteran discounts and services. Most Ohio counties issue it free; state law caps any fee at $2.
listings.eligibility: Veterans who record their discharge papers (DD-214) with the county recorder, in a county whose commissioners have authorized veteran ID cards.
listings.how_to_apply: Record your DD-214 with the county recorder, then apply in person with two current IDs, at least one with a photo. Find your county's location at ohiovets.gov/vetIDs.
listings.location: County Recorder's Office or County Veterans Service Office
listings.cost: Free in most counties; counties may charge up to $2
listings.source_title: Section 317.241 - Ohio Revised Code (veteran identification cards)
listings.notes: 'Most Ohio counties issue these free' is from the ODVS Resource Guide 2026. The ohiovets.gov/vetIDs locator did not load for us.

listings.name: County veterans burial assistance (ORC 5901.25)
listings.organization: County Veterans Service Commissions (all 88 Ohio counties)
listings.summary: When a veteran, or a veteran's parent, spouse or surviving spouse, dies without the means to pay for the funeral or cremation, the county veterans service commission contracts with a funeral director the family picks to provide burial or cremation at a fair and reasonable price.
listings.eligibility: The deceased was a veteran, or the parent, spouse or surviving spouse of a veteran, and died without the means to pay necessary funeral or cremation costs. Burial can be in any cemetery in Ohio except those used only for paupers and criminals.
listings.how_to_apply: Family or friends apply to the veterans service commission in the county and choose the funeral director; the commission contracts with that director. Contact your County Veterans Service Office before arrangements are final.
listings.location: County Veterans Service Office in each of Ohio's 88 counties
listings.source_title: Section 5901.25 - Ohio Revised Code (burial of veterans and family members)
listings.notes: The statute sets no dollar amount; each county sets its own allowance and process.

listings.name: County Veterans Service Commission Financial Assistance
listings.organization: County Veterans Service Commissions (all 88 Ohio counties), under Ohio Revised Code Chapter 5901
listings.summary: Every Ohio county has a veterans service commission, funded by a county levy, that gives temporary emergency financial help to veterans and their families who are in need. Each county commission decides what it pays for and how much.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, active-duty service members, and their spouses, surviving spouses, dependent parents, minor children or wards, who have lived in the county at least three months (ORC 5901.08). Guard and Reserve members called to active duty by presidential order or act of Congress, and their spouses and dependents, can get immediate help until their military pay or benefits start (ORC 5901.15). Need-based rules are set by each county.
listings.how_to_apply: Call or visit the County Veterans Service Office in the county where you live. Bring your DD-214 and proof of your income and bills; the county office will tell you what else it needs.
listings.location: County Veterans Service Office in each of Ohio's 88 counties
listings.source_title: Section 5901.08 - Ohio Revised Code (eligibility for county veterans financial assistance)
listings.notes: Also read: ORC 5901.15 (immediate assistance for activated Guard/Reserve) and the ODVS Resource Guide 2026, which describes this as 'temporary emergency financial assistance' at County Veterans Service Offices. What expenses are covered (rent, utilities, food, etc.) and award limits vary by county and were not published on a statewide page we could read. The dvs.ohio.gov CVSO directory page did not load for us; the URL is printed on ODVS's own materials. Phone is the ODVS toll-free line (877-OHIO-VET).

listings.name: County Veterans Service Office: free help with VA claims and benefits
listings.organization: County Veterans Service Offices (all 88 Ohio counties) with the Ohio Department of Veterans Services
listings.summary: Accredited county veterans service officers help veterans and families file and manage federal VA claims, such as disability compensation, pension and survivor benefits, and connect them to local and state resources, at no cost.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members, and their family members and survivors who live in the county.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact your County Veterans Service Office to set up an appointment; bring your DD-214 and any VA letters. Find your county office in the ODVS CVSO directory.
listings.location: County Veterans Service Office in each of Ohio's 88 counties
listings.source_title: Ohio Department of Veterans Services Resource Guide 2026
listings.notes: Resource guide also lists county office phone numbers (for example Franklin 614-525-2500, Cuyahoga 216-698-2600, Montgomery 937-225-4801).

listings.name: Cuyahoga County Homeless Stand Down
listings.summary: Cleveland's joint homeless stand down serving veterans and non-veterans, with goods and services from many providers and a veterans section with boots, coats and socks in past years.
listings.eligibility: People experiencing homelessness, including veterans (details not verified).
listings.how_to_apply: Attend on event day; check the Cuyahoga County events calendar for the next date.
listings.deadline: Held in April in recent years (April 26, 2025, 10 a.m.-2 p.m., Cleveland Public Auditorium). 2027 date not published.
listings.location: Cleveland Public Auditorium (2024 and 2025)
listings.source_title: Homeless Stand Down - Cuyahoga County
listings.notes: Seen only in search excerpts; county page not read in full. A separate VetConnect/Veteran Stand Down was held Sept. 21, 2024 at the Cuyahoga County Welcome Center.

listings.name: 2026 Christmas Toy Drive for Veteran Families
listings.organization: Delaware County Veteran Services and DAV Chapter 79
listings.summary: Holiday toy drive collecting toys and gift cards for Delaware County veteran families in need.
listings.eligibility: Delaware County veteran families in need (criteria not published).
listings.how_to_apply: Call the Veteran Services Office at 740-833-2010 to ask about receiving help. Donations are taken at the office and at drop-off events through Dec. 12, 2026.
listings.location: Delaware County Veteran Services Office, 91 N. Sandusky St., Delaware, plus Powell drop-off events
listings.source_title: 2026 Christmas Toy Drive - Delaware County Veteran Services
listings.notes: The page describes the donation side; how families sign up to receive toys is not published, so the listing says to call the office.

listings.name: Delaware County Veteran Financial Assistance and Dental Programs
listings.summary: Needs-based help: payment of monthly bills such as rent or mortgage and emergency home or car repairs; $400 in gift cards each quarter for lower-income households; and dental cleanings or emergency dental care.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with active duty service (reserve or guard training time doesn't count), honorable or under-honorable-conditions discharge, Delaware County resident 90+ days; qualifying surviving spouses and dependents. Household income at or below 300% of poverty (bills and repairs), 150% (quarterly gift cards) or 250% (dental), and expenses must exceed net income.
listings.how_to_apply: Call 740-833-2010 for current program details and an appointment. Bring the application, photo ID, DD214, proof of 90-day residency, proof of income, 60 days of bank statements and proof expenses exceed income (two estimates for repairs).
listings.location: Historic Courthouse, ground floor, 91 N. Sandusky St., Delaware, OH 43015
listings.source_title: Financial Assistance - Delaware County Veteran Services
listings.notes: Dental eligibility must be verified with the office before going to a dentist.

listings.name: Delaware County Veteran Transportation
listings.summary: Rides to VA medical facilities within 50 miles and VA referral appointments; with extended scheduling, also non-VA medical visits, senior enrichment activities and local necessity trips. All veterans can also get Delaware County Transit bus passes.
listings.eligibility: Delaware County veterans with no other means of transportation or who can't drive for medical reasons.
listings.how_to_apply: Call 740-833-2012, Monday to Friday 8 a.m.-4 p.m., at least three business days (72 hours) ahead; you can leave a message any time.
listings.deadline: Book at least 3 business days ahead
listings.location: Delaware County, OH
listings.source_title: Transportation - Delaware County Veteran Services
listings.notes: Requests the office can't fill are referred to Delaware County Transit.

listings.name: Visiting Vets / Veteran Services Volunteer
listings.summary: Volunteers make companionship visits to Delaware County veterans one or two times a week and help plan and run county veteran events.
listings.eligibility: Adults with reliable transportation who complete onboarding, including a drug screen and background check.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through the county's 'Veteran Services Volunteer' posting, linked from the Delaware County Veteran Services home page.
listings.location: Visits at varying locations in Delaware County
listings.source_title: Delaware County Veteran Services
listings.notes: The county home page shows the Visiting Vets flyer and links the volunteer posting, but the posting page blocks automated reading; duties and requirements come from search excerpts of job-board copies.

listings.name: Flag City Honor Flight
listings.summary: Honor Flight hub in Findlay that flies veterans from Toledo Express Airport to Washington, D.C., to see their war memorials.
listings.eligibility: WWII, Korean War era and Vietnam era veterans may apply, and veterans who served through July 31, 1991 are encouraged to apply. WWII, Korea, Vietnam and terminally ill veterans get priority; selection is by conflict, age and application date.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply on the Veterans page. Once you have applied you do not need to apply again.
listings.deadline: Three flights planned for 2027; dates to be released
listings.location: Flights leave Toledo Express Airport; mailing address PO Box 885, Findlay, OH 45839
listings.source_title: Flag City Honor Flight
listings.notes: Serves Northwest Ohio and Southeast Michigan; no county list published. The site says there is a wait list and applicants are not guaranteed a 2027 seat (size not published). Cost not stated on pages read. Email info@flagcityhonorflight.org.

listings.name: Preventive Dental Program
listings.summary: County dental program for lower-income Franklin County veterans and their spouses.
listings.eligibility: Honorably separated veterans, their spouses and surviving spouses who have lived in Franklin County at least 90 days, with household income at or below 250% of the federal poverty level.
listings.how_to_apply: Email vsc.dental@franklincountyohio.gov or call the commission's main line.
listings.location: Memorial Hall, Room 100, 280 E. Broad St., Columbus, OH 43215
listings.source_title: Preventive Dental Program - Franklin County, Ohio
listings.notes: Covered services, limits and any copay are not published on the page.

listings.name: Temporary Financial Assistance
listings.summary: Short-term, needs-based financial help for Franklin County veterans facing an immediate need, meant as a bridge, not an entitlement.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with an honorable discharge who have lived in Franklin County at least 90 days and show verified financial need. May request once every 30 days.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the Financial Assistance Request Form and send it with required documents to vsc.intake@franklincountyohio.gov or the Memorial Hall drop box. Every applicant has an interview; reviews take up to three business days. Walk-in and same-day appointments are not available.
listings.location: Memorial Hall, Room 100, 280 E. Broad St., Columbus, OH 43215
listings.source_title: Financial Assistance - Franklin County, Ohio
listings.notes: Requests needing commission approval require attending the Wednesday 9 a.m. meeting in person.

listings.name: Free hunting and fishing licenses for disabled veterans and former POWs
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife (eligibility certified by Ohio Department of Veterans Services)
listings.summary: Ohio resident veterans who are permanently and totally disabled, hold disabled veteran plates, or are former POWs get free fishing and hunting licenses, fur taker permits, deer and wild turkey permits and the wetlands habitat stamp. Approval lasts five years.
listings.eligibility: Ohio resident for the last six consecutive months and one of: honorably discharged with a VA permanent and total disability and receiving VA pension or compensation; holding Ohio Disabled Veterans license plates (ORC 4503.41); or a former prisoner of war with an honorable discharge.
listings.how_to_apply: Complete form DNR 9032-B and send it to ODVS Eligibility Verifications, 1240 East Ninth Street, Room 1357, Cleveland, OH 44199-2001, fax 216-522-4844 or email liaisonoffice@dvs.ohio.gov. After you get your approval letter, pick up your free licenses each year from a license agent or online.
listings.deadline: Rolling; approval lasts 5 years, licenses must be picked up each license year (ends last day of February)
listings.location: Online or by mail
listings.source_title: Disabled Veterans & Former POWs 5-Year Free License Application (DNR 9032-B)
listings.notes: Legal basis ORC 1533.12(B), current version effective March 20, 2026 (read). Residents of Ohio military homes also get a free annual fishing license under ORC 1533.12(B)(3).

listings.name: Ohio GI Promise (in-state tuition for veterans and military families)
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Higher Education and Ohio public colleges
listings.summary: Veterans, active-duty service members, and their spouses and dependents can be charged Ohio in-state tuition at Ohio public colleges, without the usual one-year residency wait, if they meet the law's service conditions.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with at least one year of active duty and an honorable (or service-related medical) discharge who live in Ohio at the start of the term; or GI Bill (Post-9/11 or Montgomery) users with at least 90 days of active duty living in Ohio; recipients of transferred GI Bill or Fry Scholarship benefits; active-duty members and their spouses and dependents while on active duty; and spouses and dependents of veterans killed on duty, MIA or POW.
listings.how_to_apply: Ask the admissions, registrar or veterans services office at your Ohio public college to classify you as an Ohio resident under the GI Promise; bring your DD-214 or orders and proof you live in Ohio.
listings.deadline: Before the start of the term
listings.location: Ohio public colleges and universities
listings.source_title: Section 3333.31 - Ohio Revised Code (residency for tuition purposes)
listings.notes: Also read the ODHE Education for Veterans page, which names the Ohio GI Promise and gives the 614-466-6000 line.

listings.name: Heroes on the Water - Southwest Ohio Chapter
listings.summary: Free kayak fishing days on lakes around Cincinnati; the chapter provides kayaks, fishing gear and safety gear, and no experience is needed.
listings.eligibility: Active-duty military, veterans, law enforcement officers, first responders and their family members.
listings.how_to_apply: Email the chapter at Southwest.OH@heroesonthewater.org with your name, contact information and interest; the chapter follows up.
listings.deadline: Upcoming event dates listed as 'coming soon'
listings.location: Grant Lake, Lake Barber, East Fork State Park and lakes within 15 miles of Cincinnati
listings.source_title: Southwest Ohio - Heroes on the Water

listings.name: Ohio Hidden Heroes Scholarship (caregivers of disabled veterans)
listings.organization: Participating Ohio colleges and universities, under Ohio Revised Code 3333.421
listings.summary: Participating Ohio colleges waive the instructional and general fees left after other aid, and give a textbook stipend, to caregivers of veterans with a 100% service-connected disability. Schools also help with credit transfer and may award credit for caregiving experience.
listings.eligibility: A person enrolled as a family caregiver in the VA Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers who cares for a veteran with a 100% service-connected disability, enrolling at an Ohio institution that has set up the program.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply to a participating college with a letter of eligibility from the VA. ODHE keeps a list of schools that offer the program.
listings.location: Participating Ohio colleges and universities
listings.source_title: Section 3333.421 - Ohio Revised Code (Ohio hidden hero scholarship program)
listings.notes: Participation is optional for each school; the ODHE Hidden Heroes page listing participating schools did not load for us. Phone is the ODHE main line from the ODVS resource guide. No participation counts are required to be reported.

listings.name: High school diplomas for veterans (ORC 3313.616)
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Veterans Services and Ohio school districts
listings.summary: Ohio school districts and chartered nonpublic schools can award a high school diploma to World War II, Korea and Vietnam veterans who left school before graduating to serve, including posthumously to a living relative.
listings.eligibility: Honorably discharged World War II, Korean conflict or Vietnam conflict veterans who left high school before graduating to serve in the armed forces or because of family circumstances, and who live in Ohio or attended an Ohio high school. Women who left school in those eras to join the workforce or war effort also qualify.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact your County Veterans Service Office, which helps apply under ODVS rules.
listings.location: Your County Veterans Service Office and local school district
listings.source_title: Section 3313.616 - Ohio Revised Code (diplomas for veterans)
listings.notes: 'Contact your CVSO' instruction comes from the ODVS Resource Guide 2026.

listings.name: Enhanced Homestead Exemption for Disabled Veterans
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Taxation and county auditors
listings.summary: A property tax reduction on the home of a veteran rated 100% disabled by the VA, with no income limit. Surviving spouses who keep living in the home may also qualify.
listings.eligibility: Veteran with a VA total (100%) service-connected disability rating, or 100% compensation for individual unemployability, discharged under honorable conditions, who owns and lives in the home as a principal residence on January 1 of the filing year; or the surviving spouse. Homes owned by a corporation, partnership or LLC do not qualify.
listings.how_to_apply: File form DTE 105I with your county auditor with a copy of your DD-214 and your VA rating letter.
listings.deadline: File with the county auditor on or before December 31 of the tax year
listings.location: Your county auditor's office
listings.source_title: Taxes - Ohio Department of Veterans Services
listings.notes: The ODVS page (read) confirms 100% service-connected disabled veterans and surviving spouses, tax years 2014 and later. The DTE 105I rules, December 31 deadline and the tax year 2026 amount (taxes on $59,400 of market value, up from $58,000 in TY2025, indexed to inflation) come from tax.ohio.gov pages we could see only in search excerpts; the tax.ohio.gov FAQ and form did not load. Confirm amount with the county auditor.

listings.name: Honor Flight Cleveland
listings.summary: All-expense-paid day trip from Cleveland to Washington, D.C., memorials, with round-trip airfare (CLE to BWI), chartered bus, parking, meals, polo shirt and cap.
listings.eligibility: U.S. veterans. Seats go first-come, first-served with WWII veterans first, then Korean War, Vietnam and all others. A guardian goes with any veteran who uses or needs mobility equipment.
listings.how_to_apply: Submit the online veteran application from the Applications page; you are placed in the queue for the next available flight. Terminally ill veterans can ask about the TLC Program.
listings.deadline: Rolling. Flying season usually runs May through November; 2027 dates not yet posted.
listings.location: Flights leave Cleveland Hopkins (CLE); mailing address P.O. Box 119, Elyria, OH
listings.source_title: Applications - Honor Flight Cleveland
listings.notes: Serves Northeast Ohio; county list not published (the site's 'Counties Served' and 'Veterans Flown' counters did not render). No phone on the site.

listings.name: Honor Flight Columbus
listings.summary: Free one-day trip from Columbus to Washington, D.C., to see the war memorials. Each veteran is paired with a trained volunteer guardian.
listings.eligibility: Veterans who served on or before July 31, 1991 (the FAQ also says age 65 or older). WWII and Korean War veterans and terminally ill veterans get top priority; terminally ill veterans are booked on the first available seat through the TLC Program. Non-veteran spouses cannot go.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online from the Veteran Application page, or print the paper application and mail it. Everyone else goes on a first-come, first-served waitlist.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time. 2027 flight schedule not yet released; next mission to be announced in December 2026.
listings.location: Flights leave from John Glenn Columbus International Airport (CMH)

capacity.served: 11,413 senior veterans flown to Washington to date (cumulative, 2026 season ran March 25 to November 10, 2026)

listings.source_title: About | HonorFlightColumbus
listings.notes: Serves 40 counties; any eligible veteran who can get to CMH may also apply. The About page (served on or before July 31, 1991) and the FAQ (age 65+) word eligibility differently. About page gave 'over 11,260' as of spring 2026; flight schedule page later shows 11,413. Waitlist size not published.

listings.name: Honor Flight Dayton
listings.summary: Free trip from Dayton to Washington, D.C., to visit the national war memorials, including airfare, bus transportation in D.C., meals and a t-shirt.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with active duty service between Dec. 7, 1941 and May 7, 1975. WWII veterans and terminally ill veterans from those years get top priority; terminally ill veterans of any conflict are scheduled for the next flight. Eligible veteran spouses may fly on the same flight; widows and non-veteran spouses cannot go.
listings.how_to_apply: Fill out the Veteran Application on the Applications page. Veterans fly on a first-come, first-served basis.
listings.location: Flights leave from and return to Dayton International Airport
listings.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions - Honor Flight Dayton
listings.notes: Counties served not published. No phone on the site; office email hfdoffice@woh.rr.com. The November 2026 reunion was cancelled. Wheelchairs provided; veterans on oxygen bring a concentrator and backup battery.

listings.name: Honor Flight Dayton RVC Program (Recreational Vehicle Convoy)
listings.summary: For eligible veterans who would rather not fly: a motor-home convoy to Washington, D.C., with two travel days, a one-day memorial tour, two hotel nights and a welcome-home reception. Transportation, meals and a t-shirt are free.
listings.eligibility: Same service dates as the flights (Dec. 7, 1941 to May 7, 1975, or terminally ill). Veterans must be able to walk, climb into a motor home and tour bus several times, stay in a hotel and handle personal needs with minimal help.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact the RVC trip coordinator through the RVC Program page (rvc@honorflightdayton.org). The general Veteran Application is on the Applications page.
listings.deadline: Next convoy date to be announced (listed as TBD)
listings.location: Leaves from the Fairborn Holiday Inn, Fairborn, OH
listings.source_title: Honor Flight Dayton RVC Program
listings.notes: Counties served not published. The page does not say whether the general veteran application covers the RVC.

listings.name: Honor Flight Tri-State
listings.summary: Free one-day trip from the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky airport to Washington, D.C., memorials for veterans 65 and older.
listings.eligibility: Veterans age 65 or older with any U.S. military service, stateside or overseas. Needs a Real ID or passport and the ability to climb six bus steps about 14 times in an 18-hour day; veterans who rely fully on a wheelchair are pointed to the Flightless Honor Flight.
listings.how_to_apply: Open a veteran account on the Veteran's Page and submit the online form. Veterans wait by age, oldest first; selected veterans are notified only by email and text.
listings.deadline: Rolling, apply any time. 2027 flight dates not posted.
listings.location: Flights leave Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport (CVG) for Reagan National (DCA)
listings.source_title: FAQs | Honor Flight Tri-State
listings.notes: Serves the Greater Cincinnati tri-state area (Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana); county list not published.

listings.name: Flightless Honor Flight
listings.summary: A local, two-hour Honor Flight-style day for veterans who can't travel: welcome ceremony, color guard and bagpipers, mail call, virtual memorial tour, refreshments and a welcome-home celebration.
listings.eligibility: Veterans 65 and older, wartime or peacetime, stateside or overseas, who can't take a regular Honor Flight for medical or logistical reasons. A guardian is assigned if the veteran has none.
listings.how_to_apply: Download and complete the Flightless Honor Flight application on the program page. Spots are limited and filled first-come, first-served depending on venue size.
listings.location: Indoor venue in the Cincinnati area (announced per event)
listings.source_title: Flightless Honor Flight | Honor Flight Tri-State
listings.notes: Counties not published. Slot count not published (depends on venue).

listings.name: Hunt and fish without a license while home on military leave
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Wildlife
listings.summary: Active-duty service members home on leave or furlough can fish, hunt and trap in Ohio without a license, permit or stamp, and those stationed in Ohio can buy resident-rate licenses whatever their home state.
listings.eligibility: Members of the armed forces on active duty who are on leave or furlough (must carry a card or other evidence of active duty). Deer and wild turkey still require the permit, sold at the resident rate with no hunting license needed. Active-duty members stationed in Ohio qualify for resident licenses.
listings.how_to_apply: No application: carry your military ID or leave papers while hunting or fishing. Buy any needed deer or turkey permit from a license agent or online.
listings.location: Statewide
listings.cost: Free (deer and turkey permits at resident rate)
listings.source_title: Section 1533.12 - Ohio Revised Code (free licenses and military exemptions)
listings.notes: Current version effective March 20, 2026 (HB 247).

listings.name: Controlled Hunt Program for Veterans with Service-Connected Disabilities
listings.summary: Controlled archery deer hunt on Lake Metroparks' Big Creek Williams Rd. property, reserved for veterans with service-connected disabilities.
listings.eligibility: U.S. armed forces veterans with a service-connected disability, age 18 or older. Lake Metroparks employees and their household members are not eligible. Participants complete archery proficiency testing.
listings.how_to_apply: Applications for the 2026-2027 hunt are closed. Watch the program page for the next application period or call Registration.
listings.deadline: 2026-2027 applications closed; next application period not yet published
listings.location: Big Creek Williams Rd. property; proficiency testing at Hidden Lake archery range, 7024 Kniffen Rd., Leroy Twp.
listings.source_title: Wildlife Management Program - Veterans w/SCD | Lake Metroparks
listings.notes: A lottery may be used if applicants exceed available slots; slot count not published. Open to veterans who can reach Lake County, not only residents.

listings.name: Military Injury Relief Fund (MIRF)
listings.summary: A tax-exempt $500 grant for Ohio service members and veterans injured in combat, or diagnosed with post-traumatic stress, while serving after October 7, 2001. Eligible people can receive one grant per Ohio fiscal year for up to three fiscal years, first come, first served while fund money lasts.
listings.eligibility: Ohio resident at the time of application, injured in active service after October 7, 2001, proven by a Purple Heart, a combat-related injury with a Combat Action Ribbon or Combat Action Badge, or another combat-related injury such as traumatic brain injury or an IED blast injury; or diagnosed with PTSD while serving after October 7, 2001 (medical diagnosis required).
listings.how_to_apply: Complete the ODVS MIRF application and sign it in front of a notary. Attach your DD-214 (active duty: a Leave and Earnings Statement; Guard/Reserve: Title 10 activation orders), proof of Ohio residency and injury documents, and mail to Ohio Department of Veterans Services, Attn: MIRF, P.O. Box 373, Sandusky, OH 44871.
listings.deadline: Rolling; one grant per Ohio fiscal year, awarded first come, first served while money in the fund lasts
listings.location: Online or by mail
listings.source_title: Rule 5902-8-02 - Ohio Administrative Code (Military Injury Relief Fund grants)
listings.notes: Also read: the ODVS MIRF page (dvs.ohio.gov/veteran-benefits/benefits-resources/military-injury-relief-fund) and the 2024 MIRF application. Amount ($500), one grant per fiscal year for up to three fiscal years, and first-come basis come from the administrative rule (effective Feb 28, 2023). Incomplete applications are returned. Denials can be appealed to the ODVS director within 60 days.

listings.name: Ohio income tax deduction for military retirement pay
listings.summary: Ohio does not tax military retirement pay: retirees deduct pay from service in the uniformed services, reserve components or Ohio National Guard on the Ohio Schedule of Adjustments. MIRF grants and veterans' disability severance pay are also not taxed.
listings.eligibility: Ohio taxpayers receiving retired pay for service in the uniformed services, reserves or Ohio National Guard. If the pension comes from a plan such as the federal civil service retirement system, only the part based on military service qualifies.
listings.how_to_apply: Claim the deduction on the Ohio Schedule of Adjustments when you file your Ohio IT 1040.
listings.deadline: With your Ohio income tax return each year
listings.location: Online or by mail
listings.source_title: Military Servicemembers and Ohio Income Taxes
listings.notes: Military questions: Military-Info@tax.state.oh.us. Same page notes the Ohio Veterans Bonus is not taxable.

listings.name: Fee-free temporary occupational license for service members and military spouses
listings.organization: Ohio state licensing agencies, under Ohio Revised Code 4743.041
listings.summary: Service members and military spouses who hold a valid license in good standing from another state can get an Ohio temporary license, valid up to six years, with all fees waived.
listings.eligibility: Holds a valid license in good standing in another state or jurisdiction, and the applicant or their spouse is on military duty in Ohio (active duty, active guard and reserve, or military technician). Criminal records checks apply where required.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply to the Ohio licensing board for your profession with proof of your out-of-state license and military orders for you or your spouse.
listings.location: The Ohio licensing board for your trade or profession
listings.source_title: Section 4743.041 - Ohio Revised Code (temporary licenses for military members and spouses)
listings.notes: Effective March 20, 2025. Applies while on military duty in Ohio; does not separately cover veterans.

listings.name: Ohio Military Veteran Educators Program (OMVEP) and educator license fee waivers
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce
listings.summary: Helps veterans, service members and military families become Ohio teachers, including through the Alternative Military Educator License and Junior ROTC instructor licenses, and waives educator license fees on several license paths.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members and eligible military family members pursuing an Ohio educator license.
listings.how_to_apply: Contact OMVEP or fill out its interest form on the Department of Education and Workforce military families page; fee waivers are requested through OMVEP.
listings.location: Online
listings.source_title: Educator License Fees Elimination for Veterans and Active Duty - Ohio Department of Education and Workforce
listings.notes: License paths with fee waivers listed: educator preparation program, Alternative Resident Educator (incl. Alternative Military Educator License), Career Technical Workforce Development, substitute, out-of-state, alternative principal, Junior ROTC instructor. Exact eligibility for waivers is on an OMVEP financial resources page we did not read. Email OhioMVEP@education.ohio.gov.

listings.name: Ohio National Guard Scholarship Program (ONGSP)
listings.organization: Ohio National Guard / Ohio Adjutant General's Department
listings.summary: Pays 100% of tuition at participating Ohio public colleges (after federal aid), or the state average public tuition rate at private schools, for enlisted Ohio Army and Air National Guard members; covers associate, bachelor's, nursing diploma and approved trade or licensing programs.
listings.eligibility: Enlisted members in good standing of the Ohio Army or Air National Guard for the whole term (and certain former members with qualifying deployment time), with a high school diploma or GED and no bachelor's degree, taking at least 3 semester hours at an approved school. Six-year enlistments earn 96 units; three- to five-year enlistments earn 48 units.
listings.how_to_apply: Request a student account at ongsp.ohio.gov, activate it with the PIN you receive, apply for federal Tuition Assistance or Credentialing Assistance first, then submit your application through the portal.
listings.deadline: Up to your school's last no-penalty add/drop date each term; applications are reviewed starting 60 days before the term
listings.location: Online
listings.source_title: Ohio National Guard Education Benefits
listings.notes: Phone from the ODVS Resource Guide 2026. Former members with deployment time are called 'Latta Amendment students' on the ONG page. ODHE describes ONGSP as paying 100% of tuition and general fees at state universities.

listings.name: Callsign ECHO: Gaming. Connection. Camaraderie.
listings.summary: Free afternoon of casual gaming and multiplayer challenges to meet other veterans and military families; part of the museum's ECHO wellness initiative.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members, military families and the community. No gaming experience needed.
listings.how_to_apply: Register online from the event page.
listings.location: National Veterans Memorial and Museum, 300 W. Broad St., Columbus
listings.source_title: Callsign ECHO - National Veterans Memorial and Museum
listings.notes: Supported by the Bob Woodruff Foundation and Discord.

listings.name: NVMM ECHO (Engage, Connect, Honor, Overcome)
listings.summary: Veteran wellness and community initiative that runs hands-on, non-clinical activities with partners: fitness and movement groups, adaptive sports, yoga and recovery, arts, leadership, financial literacy and VA benefits guidance, plus a VA Whole Health collaboration.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and community members; the page says access should not depend on income.
listings.how_to_apply: Use the Connect With Us link on the ECHO page or sign up for museum email updates; individual events are posted on the museum calendar.
listings.deadline: Ongoing; events posted on the museum calendar
listings.location: National Veterans Memorial and Museum, Columbus
listings.cost: Not published (partners aim to reduce cost barriers)
listings.source_title: NVMM ECHO - National Veterans Memorial and Museum

listings.name: Free admission for veterans
listings.summary: Free admission to the National Veterans Memorial and Museum in Columbus for veterans, active-duty members and Gold Star families.
listings.eligibility: U.S. military veterans, active-duty military members and Gold Star families. Show a Veteran ID, military ID, DD214 or driver's license marked with military status.
listings.how_to_apply: Show proof of service at arrival.
listings.location: 300 W. Broad St., Columbus, OH 43215
listings.source_title: Tickets - National Veterans Memorial and Museum
listings.notes: Regular adult admission is $18. Guests of the veteran pay regular admission.

listings.name: Military to Civilian Leadership Certificate
listings.organization: National Veterans Memorial and Museum with Ohio State University John Glenn College of Public Affairs
listings.summary: Competitive 12-week graduate certificate (six credit hours at Ohio State) with in-person sessions in Columbus, for veterans and others moving into civilian leadership roles.
listings.eligibility: Public or private sector employees with at least a bachelor's degree who served in the military, are a family member using VA education benefits, or work for a military or veteran service organization.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through the 'Learn More & Apply' link to Ohio State's Glenn College on the program page; applicants are notified by email.
listings.deadline: Applications for the Jan. 11 to Apr. 23, 2027 cohort closed Nov. 11, 2026. Next cycle not published.
listings.location: Ohio State campus or the museum, Columbus
listings.cost: $5,578 tuition (VA education benefits or employer aid may help)
listings.source_title: Higher Education - National Veterans Memorial and Museum
listings.notes: Sponsored by Columbus Downtown Development Corporation. Participant counts not published.

listings.name: Military training counts toward Ohio occupational licenses
listings.organization: Ohio state licensing agencies, under Ohio Revised Code 5903.03
listings.summary: Ohio licensing boards must treat military training and a military specialty as meeting a license's education and experience requirements when they are substantially equivalent, and licenses held by people on active duty get renewal and continuing-education allowances.
listings.eligibility: License applicants who completed a military training program and were awarded a military primary specialty substantially equivalent to the license requirement, and served in it under honorable conditions for an equivalent time.
listings.how_to_apply: When applying for an Ohio license, give the licensing board your military training records and specialty (for example your Joint Services Transcript and DD-214) and ask for military equivalency.
listings.location: The Ohio licensing board for your trade or profession
listings.source_title: Section 5903.03 - Ohio Revised Code (military training and licensing)
listings.notes: Related: ORC 4743.04 ties license renewal and continuing education during active duty to ORC 5903.10 and 5903.12.

listings.name: ODVS military discharge records (DD-214 copies)
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Veterans Services Records Office
listings.summary: ODVS keeps copies of discharge papers, from roughly the early-to-mid 1990s on, for veterans who enlisted from Ohio and asked for copies to be sent to the state, and will send copies on request.
listings.eligibility: Veterans who enlisted from Ohio and had discharge copies sent to the state (and others entitled to request their records).
listings.how_to_apply: Call 877-644-6838, fax 614-387-7317, or use the ODVS records request page.
listings.location: Online, by phone or fax
listings.source_title: Ohio Department of Veterans Services Resource Guide 2026
listings.notes: Phone and fax and the request page URL come from the ODVS veterans services poster (dam.assets.ohio.gov, read). Request page itself not read.

listings.name: Ohio Heroes home loan program
listings.summary: A discounted mortgage interest rate for veterans, active-duty military, reserve members and surviving spouses (and other public-service workers) buying a home in Ohio, with optional down payment assistance of 3% (conventional) or 3.5% (FHA, VA, USDA) of the price, forgiven after seven years.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, active-duty military, reserve component members and surviving spouses who meet OHFA income and purchase price limits, credit score of 640+ (Conventional, USDA, VA) or 650+ (FHA), and debt-to-income limits. OHFA programs serve buyers who have not owned a primary residence in the last three years (Next Home serves prior owners). Free homebuyer education required.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through an OHFA-approved lender, credit union or mortgage company; find one on the OHFA lender search.
listings.location: Through OHFA-approved lenders statewide
listings.cost: Loan program (no fee to OHFA listed); down payment assistance must be repaid if you sell within seven years
listings.source_title: Ohio Heroes - Ohio Housing Finance Agency
listings.notes: Down payment assistance terms read on myohiohome.org/downpaymentassistance.aspx; first-time buyer definition from myohiohome.org/faqs.aspx. Income and price limits are on ohiohome.org/limits (not read). The page does not say how big the rate discount is.

listings.name: OHIOCares / Ohio National Guard Family Readiness & Warrior Support
listings.organization: Ohio National Guard and State of Ohio
listings.summary: A statewide helpline and website that connects Ohio veterans, service members and military families to behavioral health care and support services.
listings.eligibility: Ohio veterans, service members and their families.
listings.how_to_apply: Call 800-761-0868 or visit ohiocares.ohio.gov.
listings.location: Statewide, by phone or online
listings.source_title: Ohio Department of Veterans Services Resource Guide 2026
listings.notes: ohiocares.ohio.gov did not load for us; services listed only by name in the ODVS Resource Guide 2026 (Behavioral Health and Ohio National Guard sections).

listings.name: Project Healing Waters Fly Fishing - Ohio programs
listings.organization: Project Healing Waters Fly Fishing, Inc.
listings.summary: Free fly fishing, fly tying and casting programs and one-day or multi-day fishing trips for disabled veterans and service members, run by local volunteer programs. All equipment provided.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with a VA disability rating, or referred by VA staff, or holding a military service rating while awaiting a VA rating. Active and reserve service members who were wounded, ill or injured on active duty and are referred by their military health care provider.
listings.how_to_apply: Find the nearest Ohio program on the Locations page and contact it through the site's contact form or FieldSupportAdmin@ProjectHealingWaters.org. No application form.
listings.location: Programs in Sheffield Village, Akron, Cleveland, Rocky River and Columbus/Central Ohio

capacity.served: 6,056 injured and disabled service members and veterans served nationwide in 2023 (183 programs)

listings.source_title: FAQs : Project Healing Waters
listings.notes: Counties are where the five listed Ohio programs are based, not an official service-area list. Served figure is national, not Ohio-only. The Columbus program has hosted about 30 events a year (2022 NVMM page).

listings.name: Ohio Safety Officers College Memorial Fund (military families)
listings.summary: Pays college costs for the children and spouses of U.S. armed forces members killed in the line of duty in Operation Enduring Freedom, Operation Iraqi Freedom or a presidentially designated combat zone (and of Ohio safety officers killed on duty). For 2025-2026 it covers 100% of instructional and general fees at Ohio public colleges, up to $10,672 a year at private colleges, or up to $8,000 a year for certificate programs.
listings.eligibility: Child or spouse of a service member killed in the line of duty during OEF, OIF or in a designated combat zone; must be a current Ohio resident (the service member did not need to be an Ohio resident) and not qualify for the War Orphan scholarship; pursuing an associate or bachelor's degree or certificate program. Up to four academic years of study.
listings.how_to_apply: Take a copy of the marriage certificate (spouses) and a copy of the Report of Casualty to the financial aid office at a participating Ohio college, which contacts ODHE.
listings.location: Participating Ohio colleges and universities
listings.source_title: Ohio Safety Officers College Memorial Fund
listings.notes: Award figures are for 2025-2026 as published. Number of recipients not published.

listings.name: Free camping at Ohio State Parks for disabled veterans and former prisoners of war
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Parks and Watercraft
listings.summary: Disabled veterans and honorably discharged former prisoners of war who live in Ohio do not pay camping fees at Ohio State Parks. The waiver covers camping fees only, not lodges or other facilities.
listings.eligibility: Disabled veterans: Ohio residents with a VA-rated permanent and total disability who receive VA pension or compensation and were honorably discharged, or any veteran issued disabled veteran license plates under Ohio Revised Code 4503.41. Former POWs: members of the U.S. armed forces captured and held by an enemy of the United States, honorably discharged, and Ohio residents.
listings.how_to_apply: Disabled veterans carry evidence of their disability, as set by ODNR rule, while in the state park. Former POWs present written evidence such as a record of separation or a letter from a branch of the armed forces. Check ODNR's camping discounts page for the current proof rules before you book.
listings.location: Ohio State Parks campgrounds
listings.source_title: Ohio Revised Code Section 1546.05 (Exemptions and discounts from certain fees and charges), codes.ohio.gov
listings.notes: Verified from the official Ohio Revised Code page on codes.ohio.gov, section 1546.05 divisions (A), (C) and (D) (effective September 14, 2016; Senate Bill 293, 131st General Assembly). ODNR's own pages still refused our fetches, so the form of proof ODNR asks for (the earlier record described a camping pass with renewal rules) was not read; the statute itself describes no pass. Phone left blank because no page we read gives one.

listings.name: Ohio State Parks 25% discount for veterans and service members
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Parks and Watercraft
listings.summary: Ohio law now gives veterans and service members a 25 percent discount on Ohio State Parks services and rentals, such as camping and overnight stays. Merchandise is not discounted.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and service members as defined in Ohio Revised Code 5903.01 who present valid documentation. The statute as read names no Ohio residency requirement.
listings.how_to_apply: Show valid documentation when you book or check in: an Ohio veterans identification card, a Department of Defense ID (common access card, DD Form 1173 or Next Generation Uniformed Services ID), a military annual or lifetime pass for the national parks and federal recreational lands, or a VA veteran health identification card.
listings.location: Ohio State Parks campgrounds, cabins and lodges
listings.cost: 25% off park services and rentals; merchandise excluded
listings.source_title: Ohio Revised Code Section 1546.04 (Adoption of rules), codes.ohio.gov
listings.notes: Verified from the official Ohio Revised Code page on codes.ohio.gov, section 1546.04 division (B)(2) and (B)(3) (effective September 7, 2026; latest legislation listed as Senate Bill 223 and House Bill 96, 136th General Assembly; the earlier record said Senate Bill 233). The statute directs ODNR to adopt rules for the discount; ODNR's November 5, 2026 release and discounts page still refused our fetches, so ODNR's booking terms seen earlier only in search excerpts (new reservations only, not combinable, one site per period, veteran must be present) were dropped. Phone left blank because no page we read gives one.

listings.name: Laura's Summit County Stand Down
listings.summary: Annual free event for veterans with counseling, dental, vision and foot exams, haircuts, clothing and cold-weather gear, lunch, showers, VA health care sign-up, claims help, legal help and state ID help.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, with a focus on homeless and displaced veterans in Summit County. All services free.
listings.how_to_apply: Attend on event day. The free veterans dental clinic and workshops have their own sign-ups on the website. Questions by call or text.
listings.deadline: Held each September (2026 dental clinic was Sept. 14, 2026). 2027 date not yet published.
listings.location: Guy's Party Center, Akron (event site in recent years)
listings.source_title: Home - Lauras Summit County Stand Down
listings.notes: Phone is text and voicemail only. Summit County's 2023 release gives the site as Guy's Party Center, 500 E. Waterloo Rd., Akron. A 2026 report is posted as a draft infographic; figures not in text.

listings.name: Team Rubicon disaster response in Ohio
listings.summary: Veteran-founded disaster response group. Volunteers ('Greyshirts') do muck-outs, debris removal and chainsaw work for storm and flood survivors, such as the August 2026 operations in Franklin, Perry, Muskingum, Highland and Brown counties.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, first responders and community members can volunteer.
listings.how_to_apply: Sign up on the Volunteer With Us page and complete Team Rubicon's online and in-person training.
listings.location: Deployments across Ohio as disasters happen
listings.source_title: Disaster Relief Volunteers Mobilize Across Ohio and Indiana After Derechos and Floods
listings.notes: Eligibility wording from the How to Get Involved page; training and background-check steps not read on the official page.

listings.name: Team RWB Ohio chapters
listings.summary: Free veteran fitness and social community with local Ohio chapters that hold workouts, runs and events, plus app-based fitness challenges.
listings.eligibility: Veterans, service members and supporters (the site describes a community of all three).
listings.how_to_apply: Join free through the Team RWB member app or web app, then join your local Ohio chapter group.
listings.location: Chapters: Akron/Canton, Cincinnati, Cleveland, Columbus, Dayton, Firelands and Toledo
listings.source_title: Find Your Chapter - Team Red, White & Blue
listings.notes: Chapter pages sit inside the member app (members.teamrwb.org) and were not read.

listings.name: Ohio VALOR Stand Down Events
listings.summary: Community stand down days in Zanesville, Newark and Malta/McConnelsville with a free meal and help connecting veterans to VA and community services.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and community members in need; no criteria published.
listings.how_to_apply: Walk in on event day. Watch the VALOR Clinic Foundation site for the next dates.
listings.deadline: Spring 2026 events were May 16 (Zanesville and Newark) and May 30 (Malta/McConnelsville). Next dates not published.
listings.location: Zanesville, Newark and Malta/McConnelsville, OH

capacity.served: Almost 100 community members assisted and contact made with 7 veterans (spring 2026 stand downs)

listings.source_title: Ohio VALOR Spring Stand Down Events - May 16, 2026
listings.notes: Counties listed are where the events were held; the foundation does not publish a service-area list. No organization main line on the page.

listings.name: Ohio Veterans Bonus (Persian Gulf, Afghanistan, Iraq)
listings.summary: A one-time cash bonus for Ohio veterans of the Persian Gulf, Afghanistan and Iraq eras: up to $500 for service anywhere in the world or up to $1,000 for service in a designated country, with a $1,500 lifetime maximum. All application windows have now closed.
listings.eligibility: Ohio resident when entering service and when applying, with qualifying active-duty service in the Persian Gulf (1990-1991), Iraq (2003-2011) or Afghanistan (October 7, 2001 to August 30, 2021) eras.
listings.how_to_apply: Applications are no longer accepted. Questions about past applications go to ODVS.
listings.deadline: Closed: Afghanistan-era applications ended August 30, 2024; Persian Gulf and Iraq deadlines passed earlier
listings.location: Online or by mail
listings.source_title: Welcome to the Ohio Veterans Bonus Program
listings.notes: CLOSED program, kept for reference because it was requested; recommend holding back or marking closed. Bonus payments are not taxable in Ohio (tax.ohio.gov military page).

listings.name: Ohio Veterans Hall of Fame nominations
listings.summary: The Ohio Veterans Hall of Fame honors veterans who keep serving their communities after their military service; anyone can nominate a veteran for induction.
listings.eligibility: Veterans with an Ohio connection who have continued to serve their community after military service.
listings.how_to_apply: Read the criteria and submit a nomination at ohiovets.gov/HOF.
listings.location: Online or by mail
listings.source_title: Ohio Department of Veterans Services Resource Guide 2026
listings.notes: ohiovets.gov/HOF did not load for us, so the nomination deadline, criteria details and ceremony date were not verified.

listings.name: Ohio Veterans Homes (Sandusky and Georgetown)
listings.summary: Two state-run veterans homes, in Sandusky and Georgetown, offer independent living, nursing care and memory care for eligible veterans.
listings.eligibility: Eligible veterans; admission rules are set by the Ohio Veterans Homes (see ohioveteranshomes.gov).
listings.how_to_apply: Apply through ohioveteranshomes.gov or call ODVS.
listings.location: Sandusky (Erie County) and Georgetown (Brown County), Ohio
listings.source_title: Ohio Department of Veterans Services Resource Guide 2026
listings.notes: ohioveteranshomes.gov did not load for us (two tries), so bed counts, admission criteria, costs and any waitlist were not verified. Bed capacity left null.

listings.name: Cleveland Domiciliary
listings.summary: Residential care for homeless veterans on the Wade Park VA Medical Center campus, combining rehabilitative clinical services with supportive case management.
listings.eligibility: Homeless veterans (detailed criteria not published on the page read).
listings.how_to_apply: Contact Volunteers of America Ohio & Indiana through the Cleveland Domiciliary location page.
listings.location: Wade Park VA Medical Center campus, Cleveland, OH
listings.source_title: Veterans - Volunteers of America Ohio & Indiana
listings.notes: Location page itself not read (fetch budget ran out); described from the VOA veterans services page. VOA's SSVF program is excluded (already in the guide).

listings.name: Ohio War Orphan & Severely Disabled Veterans' Children Scholarship
listings.summary: Tuition aid for children of Ohio veterans who died, are missing or POW, or are severely disabled from wartime service. For 2026-2027 it pays 77% of tuition and general fees at Ohio public colleges, or $6,397 a year at private Ohio colleges.
listings.eligibility: Student age 16 to 24 at application, Ohio resident for at least the past year, full-time student at an eligible Ohio school (associate or bachelor's program at proprietary schools), with financial need and a completed FAFSA. The veteran parent served during a qualifying war period, entered service as an Ohio resident (with exceptions), and is deceased, MIA, POW, or has a 60% or higher service-connected disability (or VA permanent and total non-service-connected disability pension).
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through ODHE or mail the paper application, with the parent section notarized, plus the DD-214, VA rating letter (60%+), death certificate if applicable and the signed Student Acknowledgement Statement, to ODHE Office of Financial Aid, Attn: War Orphans Program Manager, 25 South Front St., Columbus, OH 43215.
listings.location: Online or by mail
listings.source_title: Ohio War Orphan & Severely Disabled Veterans' Children Scholarship application (ODHE)
listings.notes: Award levels from ODHE guidance memo FA 27-010 (dated July 22, 2026, updated Sept 21, 2026): 77% of tuition/general fees at public institutions; $6,397/year at private institutions for 2026-2027. Number of recipients not published in the documents we read. Program manager line 614-752-9481. The ODHE program web page did not load; application PDF and memo were read in full.

listings.name: WorkOhio / OhioMeansJobs veteran employment help
listings.organization: Ohio Department of Job and Family Services (WorkOhio, OhioMeansJobs)
listings.summary: Free one-on-one help for veterans putting military experience to work, a veteran-only job search, a Military Skills Translator, and a statewide Veterans Workforce Team that connects veterans to jobs.
listings.eligibility: Veterans looking for work in Ohio.
listings.how_to_apply: Use the WorkOhio veterans page to connect with a person or search veteran jobs, or email workohio@jfs.ohio.gov.
listings.location: Online and at OhioMeansJobs centers
listings.source_title: Veterans - WorkOhio
listings.notes: Military Skills Translator, Military Service Career Center and the Veterans Workforce Team are named in ODVS materials (Resource Guide 2026, veterans services poster). Priority of service details were not on the page we read; the OhioMeansJobs veterans page did not load.

listings.name: Burial benefit for indigent veteran families
listings.summary: A payment of up to $1,000 toward funeral costs for Butler County veteran families who are indigent or facing financial hardship.
listings.eligibility: The deceased must be a veteran, a veteran's parent or spouse, or a surviving spouse, from a Butler County family that is indigent or facing financial hardship. The funeral home's final bill, before any payments are posted, must not exceed $5,000.
listings.how_to_apply: Make an appointment with the Commission and bring the DD 214, proof of relationship if the deceased is not the veteran, the death certificate, and a detailed funeral invoice.
listings.location: 315 High Street, Hamilton, OH 45011
listings.source_title: Financial Assistance - Butler County Veterans Service Commission
listings.notes: Read the Commission's Financial Assistance page in full; the burial benefit is described there. Second published line: 513-425-8600.

listings.name: Temporary Financial Assistance
listings.summary: Temporary, need-based help for Butler County veterans and their families with housing expenses, utilities, food and hygiene items, basic living expenses, transportation, car repairs, clothing and day care. Approved applicants can also get budget counseling from LifeSpan.
listings.eligibility: Veterans and service members, and their spouses, surviving spouses, dependent parents, minor children or wards, who are bona fide Butler County residents with an Ohio state ID or driver's license. The veteran must have served at least one day of active duty outside of training, with a discharge under honorable conditions, and the household must show a definite financial need.
listings.how_to_apply: Come to the Commission office in Hamilton for a face-to-face interview, bringing the documents on the Commission's financial checklist (linked from the Financial Assistance page).
listings.location: 315 High Street, Hamilton, OH 45011
listings.source_title: Financial Assistance - Butler County Veterans Service Commission
listings.notes: Read the Commission's Financial Assistance and Eligibility pages in full. The Commission considers work income, benefits from other agencies, basic living expenses and total assets. Second published line: 513-425-8600. The ad's headline ('Free to Eligible Veterans') was about rides to VA medical facilities, but no page on bcvetsoh.gov that we could read describes a transportation program, so none is listed.

listings.name: EmpowerVetEd Scholarship
listings.summary: Lake Erie College in Painesville gives scholarships of $5,000 per year, plus an additional $5,000 per year for incidental expenses, to military-connected students in its undergraduate education preparation programs.
listings.eligibility: The college's wording: active duty, reserve, veterans, or military spouses, and veterans enrolled in any of the school's undergraduate education preparation programs. Read it as service members, veterans and military spouses studying in a Lake Erie College undergraduate education (teacher) preparation program; confirm with the college.
listings.how_to_apply: The page gives no application steps. Contact Lake Erie College's Office of Veterans and Military Service or the Office of Financial Aid through the college's main line, 440-375-7000.
listings.location: Lake Erie College, 391 W. Washington St., Painesville, OH 44077
listings.source_title: Lake Erie College - Office of Veterans and Military Service
listings.notes: Read the college's veterans page in full. The scholarship sentence is ambiguous on whether every group must be in an education preparation program; the ad described it as for those programs. No deadline, application form or funding source is published. The same page says the college takes part in the Yellow Ribbon Program and offers a veterans-only study space (The Bunker).
